questions.text: Inscript Consider a convolutional neural network that processes an input image of size 64 × 64 × 3 through the following sequence of layers: • A convolutional layer with 32 filters of size 3 × 3, stride = 1, and no padding. • A second convolutional layer with 64 filters of size 3 × 3, stride = 2, and no padding. • A flattening layer. Calculate the total number of elements in the flattened output vector.

Inscript Consider a bottleneck layer in a deep CNN where an input feature map of size 14×14×512 is processed using a 1 × 1 convolutional layer with 128 filters. Assuming each output activation requires a multiplication with each corresponding input channel value, compute the total number of multiplications required for this operation. Provide your answer in millions (e.g., write 25.5 for 25,500,000).

Inscript A YOLO v1-style object detection model divides an input image into a grid of size S ×S, where S = 7. Each grid cell predicts B = 2 bounding boxes and the model is trained to detect C = 20 object classes. Using the standard YOLO output formulation, calculate the total depth (number of channels) of the final output tensor.

Inscript In a convolutional neural network, a convolutional layer receives an input feature map with 32 channels. The layer applies 64 filters, each of spatial size 3 × 3. Assuming that each filter operates across all input channels and ignoring bias terms, calculate the total number of learnable weight parameters in this layer.
When fine-tuning large pre-trained vision models, several techniques are used to improve efficiency. Which of the following are valid strategies?
options: Mixed precision training reduces memory usage and speeds up computation.
Freezing early layers reduces the number of trainable parameters.
Using multiple data loading workers improves input pipeline efficiency.
Increasing batch size always reduces GPU memory consumption.
correct_answer: Mixed precision training reduces memory usage and speeds up computation.
Freezing early layers reduces the number of trainable parameters.
Using multiple data loading workers improves input pipeline efficiency.

questions.text: When working with PyTorch for training and deployment, proper handling of model state and devices is critical. Which of the following practices are correct?
options: Both model parameters and input tensors must be moved to the same device for computation.
Saving only the state dict is preferred for flexibility and portability.
The model architecture must be defined before loading weights using load state dict.
The state dict includes the full model architecture definition.
correct_answer: Both model parameters and input tensors must be moved to the same device for computation.
Saving only the state dict is preferred for flexibility and portability.
The model architecture must be defined before loading weights using load state dict.

questions.text: Consider the following Python code snippet using the Ultralytics YOLOv8 API: from ultralytics import YOLO model = YOLO("yolov8n.pt") for name, module in model.model.named_modules(): print(name, type(module)) Based on the architecture of YOLOv8, which of the following statements correctly describe the model?
options: The model predicts object locations directly without using predefined anchor boxes.
The model uses separate components within its detection head for classification and bounding box regression.
The model performs detection in a single forward pass without a separate proposal stage.
The model internally generates region proposals using a Region Proposal Network (RPN) before classification.
correct_answer: The model predicts object locations directly without using predefined anchor boxes.
The model uses separate components within its detection head for classification and bounding box regression.
The model performs detection in a single forward pass without a separate proposal stage.

questions.text: In training deep CNN models, different normalization and regularization techniques are used to stabilize training and improve generalization. Which of the following statements are correct?
options: Batch Normalization normalizes activations within a mini-batch to stabilize training.
Dropout randomly deactivates neurons during training to reduce overfitting.
Data augmentation artificially increases dataset diversity and improves generalization.
Batch Normalization eliminates the need for activation functions.
correct_answer: Batch Normalization normalizes activations within a mini-batch to stabilize training.
Dropout randomly deactivates neurons during training to reduce overfitting.
Data augmentation artificially increases dataset diversity and improves generalization.

questions.text: U-Net is widely used for dense prediction tasks such as segmentation and depth estimation. Which architectural components contribute to its effectiveness?
options: A symmetric encoder-decoder structure that captures both context and localization.
Skip connections that transfer high-resolution features directly to the decoder.
Upsampling operations that progressively recover spatial resolution.
Exclusive reliance on fully connected layers for prediction.
correct_answer: A symmetric encoder-decoder structure that captures both context and localization.
Skip connections that transfer high-resolution features directly to the decoder.
Upsampling operations that progressively recover spatial resolution.

questions.text: Consider the following code: model = torchvision.models.detection.fasterrcnn_resnet50_fpn(pretrained=True) images = [torch.randn(3, 600, 800)] outputs = model(images) Unlike YOLO-based models, the number of bounding boxes in outputs[0][’boxes’] varies for each image. What architectural characteristic of the model explains this behavior?
options: The model generates a variable number of region proposals based on the image content.
The model filters region proposals using confidence scores and non maximum suppression.
The model uses a fixed grid structure to predict bounding boxes.
The model predicts a constant number of bounding boxes for every image.
correct_answer: The model generates a variable number of region proposals based on the image content.
The model filters region proposals using confidence scores and non maximum suppression.

questions.text: The Inception (GoogLeNet) architecture was designed to improve computational efficiency while capturing multi-scale features. Which of the following statements correctly describe its design principles?
options: It applies multiple convolution filters of different sizes in parallel within a single module.
It uses 1 × 1 convolutions to reduce channel dimensionality before expensive operations.
It introduces auxiliary classifiers to improve gradient flow during training.
It relies solely on deep sequential stacking without parallel paths.
correct_answer: It applies multiple convolution filters of different sizes in parallel within a single module.
It uses 1 × 1 convolutions to reduce channel dimensionality before expensive operations.
It introduces auxiliary classifiers to improve gradient flow during training.

questions.text: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) differ significantly from fully connected neural networks. Which of the following mechanisms enable CNNs to efficiently process highdimensional image data?
options: Local connectivity, where neurons are connected only to a small spatial region of the input.
Parameter sharing, where the same filter is applied across different spatial locations.
Fully connected layers applied at every spatial location independently.
Removal of non-linear activation functions to simplify computation.
correct_answer: Local connectivity, where neurons are connected only to a small spatial region of the input.
Parameter sharing, where the same filter is applied across different spatial locations.

questions.text: Consider the following PyTorch code snippet: conv = torch.nn.Conv2d(3, 32, kernel_size=3, padding=1) x = torch.randn(1,3,64,64) y = conv(x) print(y.shape) Which of the following best explains the output shape?
options: Spatial dimensions reduce due to kernel size.
Padding preserves spatial dimensions while increasing channel depth to 32.
Output channels remain equal to input channels.
Convolution removes batch dimension.
questions.correct_answer: Padding preserves spatial dimensions while increasing channel depth to 32.

questions.text: Deep neural networks often suffer from degradation problems as depth increases. How do residual connections in ResNet help address this issue?
options: By reducing the number of parameters in the network.
By enabling identity mappings that allow gradients to flow more easily through deep networks.
By removing the need for activation functions.
By converting convolution layers into fully connected layers.
questions.correct_answer: By enabling identity mappings that allow gradients to flow more easily through deep networks.

questions.text: In YOLO-based object detection models, the confidence score predicted for each bounding box combines multiple factors. What does this score represent?
options: Only the probability of the predicted class.
The probability that an object exists in the box multiplied by the IoU with the ground truth.
Only the IoU between prediction and ground truth.
The distance of the object from the image center.
questions.correct_answer: The probability that an object exists in the box multiplied by the IoU with the ground truth.

questions.text: Consider the following code snippet using a YOLO-based object detection model: from ultralytics import YOLO model = YOLO("yolov8n.pt") results = model("image.jpg") boxes = results[0].boxes.xyxy print(boxes.shape) It is observed that the number of bounding boxes printed varies for different input images. Which of the following statements best explains this behavior?
options: The model divides the image into a fixed grid and always predicts a fixed number of boxes.
The model filters predictions based on confidence scores and non maximum suppression, resulting in a variable number of final detections.
The model uses a Region Proposal Network (RPN) to generate candidate regions before prediction.
The number of bounding boxes is fixed by the number of classes in the dataset.
questions.correct_answer: The model filters predictions based on confidence scores and non maximum suppression, resulting in a variable number of final detections.

questions.text: In image super-resolution models such as SRResNet, the Pixel Shuffle operation is often used for upsampling. What is the key advantage of this technique compared to naive interpolation methods?
options: It reduces the number of convolutional layers required.
It guarantees that no information is lost during downsampling.
It rearranges channel information into spatial dimensions, enabling learnable and efficient upsampling.
It performs global pooling before upsampling.
questions.correct_answer: It rearranges channel information into spatial dimensions, enabling learnable and efficient upsampling.

questions.text: In the Faster R-CNN architecture, anchors are predefined bounding boxes of different scales and aspect ratios. What is their primary role during training?
options: They serve as reference boxes that are adjusted (via regression) to match ground truth objects.
They directly output the final class predictions without further refinement.
They are only used during inference and not during training.
They replace the need for convolutional feature extraction.
questions.correct_answer: They serve as reference boxes that are adjusted (via regression) to match ground truth objects.

questions.text: In modern CNN architectures such as VGG and ResNet, it is often observed that multiple stacked 3×3 convolutional layers are used instead of a single larger convolution (e.g., 7×7). Which of the following best explains the technical advantage of this design choice?
options: It allows the network to completely eliminate the need for activation functions.
It reduces the total number of parameters while introducing additional non- linearities, improving representational power.
It ensures that the receptive field is strictly smaller than that of a larger kernel.
It guarantees that overfitting is avoided during training.
questions.correct_answer: It reduces the total number of parameters while introducing additional non- linearities, improving representational power.
